quickAnswerHtml: So Jeng is a Bib Gourmand restaurant in the MICHELIN Guide Thailand 2026, in Khon Kaen's Ban Phai area. Budget around ฿฿, and it's mostly walk-in/queue at the door

blocks.html:
The name alone is what stops people before they've even tasted the food — "So Jeng" sounds like it's poking fun at itself, but it's actually the owner's declaration of grit. He'd already failed at several businesses before deciding to open an Isan restaurant in the middle of Ban Phai district, and he named it with blunt honesty: if he goes bust again, so be it, he's not afraid. As it turns out, this one didn't go bust — it's been running for more than 40 years and has now been handed down to the second generation. And most recently, the MICHELIN Guide's 2026 edition awarded it a Bib Gourmand, confirming that this plainly decorated shophouse on Chaeng Sanit Road cooks Isan food good enough that MICHELIN inspectors drove 44 kilometres out from downtown Khon Kaen just to eat here.

What you need to order here is all about beef. Larb neua (minced beef larb) and koi neua (raw beef koi) are the duo MICHELIN singles out as the stars — full-on Isan flavour that needs no extra seasoning. Next up is tom saep neua, a hot-and-sour beef and beef offal soup that warms you from the chest out, with just the right sour-spicy kick. If you like something chewier, there's fragrant fried neua daet diao (sun-dried beef), and if you want to try something harder to find elsewhere, the mok mong mu (pork brain mok) is what locals order on repeat. All of this comes at prices low enough to run a few hundred baht a head, which is exactly why MICHELIN put this restaurant on its list of great Khon Kaen eats that won't dent your wallet.

Another draw is that the atmosphere still feels like a genuine Ban Phai neighbourhood spot — this district has long been an old junction in southern Khon Kaen where people driving between provinces pass through constantly, and So Jeng has served as a stopover for both travellers and locals for decades. Even with a MICHELIN badge on the door these days, people from around here still drop in just as often as before. The tables comfortably seat large family groups, so coming with the whole family won't feel cramped. If you're planning a road trip through Khon Kaen, or heading south toward Buri Ram–Nakhon Ratchasima, the route runs right through Ban Phai — pencil in a lunch or dinner stop here, and you'll understand exactly why a restaurant named "going bust" never will.

blocks.name: So Jeng
blocks.descHtml:
So Jeng sits on Chaeng Sanit Road in the middle of Ban Phai district, about 44 kilometres from downtown Khon Kaen, roughly a 40-minute drive. Open daily 08:00-21:00 (per MICHELIN; some local sources list 10:00-22:00, so if you're heading there very early or late, call ahead to be sure — 043-274-031 or 087-856-6877). Prices sit at ฿฿ per MICHELIN, working out to a few hundred baht per person, and the restaurant takes cash only, so come prepared.

It's walk-in only, no reservations — but don't worry about the queue, since this is a family-style shophouse restaurant that seats large groups comfortably, and there's a second Ban Phai branch nearby if the original is full. It suits self-drive travellers best, since Ban Phai sits right on the main route heading into southern Isan. Weekday lunch or dinner tends to be less packed — just walk in and order larb neua, koi neua, and tom saep with beef offal without much of a wait.
